Class HolidayRule

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.calendar.rule.HolidayRule
public class HolidayRule extends Object
A single holiday of a stock exchange, expressed as a rule that can be resolved to concrete dates for any year.

Instances are deserialized from the YAML of a trading calendar rule set. Which of the optional fields are relevant depends on type; a rule that omits a field its type requires is rejected by validate() at load time rather than silently producing wrong dates.

The validity range is essential rather than decorative. GT supports trading data back to the year 2000 and exchange holidays have changed within that window -- Juneteenth became a closure at the US exchanges only in 2021, and Euronext Paris stopped closing on Whit Monday in 2008. A rule without validFrom / validTo would therefore be wrong for a large part of the supported period.

Unknown YAML keys are rejected by the mapper configured in HolidayRuleSetYamlParser, so a misspelled field name is refused when saving instead of being silently ignored.

  • Method Details

    • resolve

      public List<LocalDate> resolve(int year)
      Resolves this rule to the dates on which the exchange is closed in the given year.

      Returns an empty list when the rule is not in force in that year, when it is a halfDay rule, or when the resolved date falls on a weekend and the observance does not transfer it. Weekend results are dropped because Saturdays and Sundays are handled separately by the trading calendar and are deliberately absent from trading_days_minus.

      Parameters:
      year - the year for which the dates are wanted
      Returns:
      the resolved closure dates, possibly empty, never null

    • resolveIgnoringHalfDayFlag

      public List<LocalDate> resolveIgnoringHalfDayFlag(int year)
      Resolves this rule to dates regardless of the halfDay flag. Used by the comparison report, which needs to know where the shortened trading days fall in order to explain disagreements; the calendar generation itself always goes through resolve(int).
      Parameters:
      year - the year for which the dates are wanted
      Returns:
      the resolved dates, possibly empty, never null

    • isValidInYear

      public boolean isValidInYear(int year)
      Whether the rule is in force in the given year according to its validity range.
      Parameters:
      year - the year to test
      Returns:
      true when the year lies within validFrom and validTo
